correctness.rationale: Lecuona--Wand's open primary text explicitly records the four-parameter nonisotopy witness and the fibered/nonfibered reordered pair, so either example alone contradicts a universal arbitrary-permutation isotopy claim. Cyclic shifts and reversal are standard universal pretzel symmetries for nonunitary parameters; their dihedral action equals \(S_3\) for three entries but has order \(2m<m!\) for \(m\ge4\). The argument correctly avoids claiming that every non-dihedral permutation changes isotopy type.
correctness.risk: Unit parameters can admit extra flype symmetries, so the stated universal symmetry boundary is deliberately restricted to nonunitary parameters.

evidence: Lecuona--Wand gives a broader warning that reordering beyond cyclic/reversal can alter isotopy type, but predates and therefore does not itself correct the 2026 theorem.
A separate SCOPE finding corrects a composite-modulus quiver formula in the same 2026 preprint, not its isotopy theorem.

value.rationale: A precise correction to a current theorem is scientifically useful even when the counterexample predates the erroneous theorem: it prevents a false isotopy symmetry from being propagated into the general pretzel-link discussion and identifies the exact reason the three-parameter case behaves differently.

final_claim: The general extension in Theorem 13 of Meng--Liu--Zhou is false: arbitrary permutation of four-or-more pretzel parameters is not a universal ambient-isotopy symmetry. The published pair \(P(3,5,7,2)\) and \(P(3,7,5,2)\) is nonisotopic, and a separate reordered pair differs in fiberedness. For nonunitary parameters, cyclic permutation and reversal are universal symmetries; these already generate all permutations only in the three-parameter case.
limitations: This audit does not reassess the preprint's independent coloring-number or coloring-quiver formulas.
The counterexamples themselves are credited to Lecuona--Wand and are not claimed as new.
